what_the_eye_sees: Hero: a snarling grotesque beast head on top of the band. It has a heavy brow, short horns and ears, a wide gaping mouth full of fangs, and two clawed paws gripping the front edge of a ledge under its chin. Spiky folded forms rise behind it. The first word is 'gargoyle', with 'snarling bulldog or foo-dog' close behind, and nothing says dragon or hood ornament any more. The wire armature from round 1 is gone; it now reads as a solid carved mass. Weaknesses: the camera meets the beast head-on, so it reads as a mask with paws over a block. The crouched body and haunches are hidden, the spout points at the lens and does not show, and the perch is a plain dark block. No cornice step, corbel or tracery can be picked out, so the 'cathedral' part of the read rests on the gargoyle alone. Face: seen from above, the head thrusts out past a squarish block, a pipe spout sticks out of the mouth along the finger, and a ridged spiny back with chevron folded wings leads to the haunches. This is the clearest waterspout read of the two views: a gargoyle jutting from a parapet. A jeweller names it 'gargoyle, Gothic' from the pair. It passes, but only just on the architecture.
changes: Perch: make the parapet read as Gothic masonry at 300 px. Give the block's front (fingertip) face and its two side faces a stepped cornice, two steps each overhanging about 0.8-1.0 mm, so they cast a hard shadow line. Taper a corbel below it into the band, and cut one blind quatrefoil or a pointed-arch panel at least 0.5 mm deep into each side face. Acceptance: in hero-300 and face-300 the block shows a lit cornice edge over a shadow band and at least one foiled or pointed recess, and does not read as a plain box.

Hero posture: turn or raise the figure so the hero camera catches the spout and some body. Thrust the head a further 1.5-2 mm past the cornice edge, lift the spout tube about 10-15 degrees above the finger axis so its tip clears the lower jaw in the hero view, and let the hunched shoulders and haunches rise above the head line behind it. Acceptance: in hero-300 the spout tip is visible projecting from the jaws, and a hunched back or haunch shows behind the head, so the beast does not read as a mask.

Wings: make the folded bat wings legible as wings and not as a spiky crest. Open the chevron ridges into two distinct ribbed membranes, each with 3-4 finger bones and scalloped trailing edges, lying along the back on either side of the spine (y about +/-2 to 3 mm). Acceptance: in face-300 two separate wing shapes with scalloped edges are visible either side of the spine.
